summary_notes: Mid-market product analytics SaaS. Primary interest: migrate from hosted API POC to Dedicated Reserved capacity for predictable SLA and cost control. Started with hosted API trial (Jan 2026) to validate latency/quality; moved to evaluation for Dedicated after 2-week POC. Price-sensitive but values reliability + VPC integration. Product lead: "User-facing assistant needs <120ms p50 on short queries; batch reranking throughput target 300 reqs/min during daily peaks." Wants deterministic cost for planning — leaning to 6- or 12-month commit. Concerned about burst headroom and overage math. Legal requires data residency for EU customers and SOC2 evidence. SE Raj ran microbenchmarks on our dedicated variant (gpt-compat-7B-q4f) — 15% cost improvement vs hosted in their profile; latency margin met at target sequence lengths (avg 64 tokens).

poC_summary: Host API POC validated models for doc-search and support flows. Key results: p50 latency 95-110ms on short queries, relevance lift +12% vs baseline embedding ranker, token consumption higher than expected due to multi-turn context. SE recommended Dedicated with autoscaling burst to handle peak reranking windows and prefix caching to reduce token usage.
pricing_discussion_notes: Mercury prefers a predictable monthly committed throughput with defined burst buffer. Exploring three commit bands: 100k tokens/day (~monthly commit 3M), 300k tokens/day (~9M), 1M tokens/day (~30M). Discussed ramp schedule: month 1 at 50% commit, month 2 at 75%, month 3 full commit; option to front-load ramp for launch. Overage rate negotiation: proposed 1.5x of base committed unit price for transient burst; Mercury requested cap on monthly overage (suggested 20% of committed). Also want explicit burst slots for scheduled marketing launches (one-off high QPS windows). Requested a trial Dedicated month with credit applied to first invoice.
